files.README.md:
# DuckDB through a Ptah plugin

This workspace starts with an empty in-memory DuckDB database. The official
provider's Go code runs inside the Ptah WebAssembly module and connects to
DuckDB-Wasm in a nested worker. Everything stays in this tab.

Preview and apply the desired schema:

    ptah schema apply --schema-file schema.sql --db-url duckdb://:memory: --dry-run
    ptah schema apply --schema-file schema.sql --db-url duckdb://:memory:
    ptah schema drift --schema-file schema.sql --db-url duckdb://:memory:

The browser engine is DuckDB v1.5.4; the native plugin release embeds v2.0.0.
Reloading or resetting discards the database.

baseline.message: This route needs schema.sql. Reset restores the workspace.

steps.title: Preview
steps.caption: Read the DuckDB plan
steps.headline: Ask Ptah for the SQL it would run.
steps.instruction: The database is empty. Preview how the official DuckDB provider would create the events table.
steps.done: The plan came from Ptah and the DuckDB provider. No table was created by the dry run.

steps.title: Apply
steps.caption: Create the events table
steps.headline: Apply the planned schema to DuckDB.
steps.instruction: Ptah asks for confirmation, then runs the provider's SQL against DuckDB-Wasm.
steps.done: The events table now exists in the live DuckDB catalog.

steps.title: Verify
steps.caption: Check for drift
steps.headline: Check that the file and DuckDB agree.
steps.instruction: Ptah reads the live catalog again and compares it with schema.sql.
steps.done: Exit 0 means Ptah found no schema drift.
